installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# MultiForge installation script
#
# Server files: /mnt/server
#
# Runs in a JDK 21 container: the MultiForge installer is a Java program, and
# MultiForge (like NeoForge 1.21.1) needs Java 21 exactly.
set -euo pipefail

apt-get update -y
apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates coreutils

mkdir -p /mnt/server
cd /mnt/server

JAVA_MAJOR=$(java -XshowSettings:properties -version 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^ *java\.specification\.version = //p' | head -n 1)
if [ "${JAVA_MAJOR}" != "21" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: the install container runs Java ${JAVA_MAJOR:-unknown}; MultiForge needs Java 21."
    exit 1
fi

REPO="https://github.com/0xnullsect0r/MultiForge/releases"
VERSION="${MULTIFORGE_VERSION#v}"
if [ "${VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
    BASE="${REPO}/latest/download"
    INSTALLER_URL="${BASE}/multiforge-installer.jar"
    ASSET="multiforge-installer.jar"
else
    BASE="${REPO}/download/v${VERSION}"
    INSTALLER_URL=$(echo "${DOWNLOAD_URL}" | sed "s/{VERSION}/${VERSION}/g")
    ASSET="multiforge-${VERSION}-installer.jar"
fi

echo "-- Downloading ${INSTALLER_URL} --"
curl -fsSL -o "${ASSET}" "${INSTALLER_URL}"

## Verify it against the release's SHA256SUMS (every release from v1.8.0 on has one).
if curl -fsSL -o SHA256SUMS "${BASE}/SHA256SUMS"; then
    EXPECTED=$(awk -v f="${ASSET}" '{ n = $2; sub(/^\*/, "", n); if (n == f) print $1 }' SHA256SUMS)
    if [ -z "${EXPECTED}" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: SHA256SUMS has no entry for ${ASSET}."
        exit 1
    fi
    echo "${EXPECTED}  ${ASSET}" | sha256sum -c -
    rm -f SHA256SUMS
else
    echo "WARNING: this release has no SHA256SUMS (older than v1.8.0); the installer was not verified."
fi

echo "-- Running the MultiForge installer --"
java -jar "${ASSET}" --installServer /mnt/server
rm -f "${ASSET}" ./*.log

## The installer lays down libraries/net/neoforged/neoforge/<v>/unix_args.txt and
## writes run.sh naming that version. A reinstall leaves older version folders
## behind, so take the one run.sh names. The startup command reads unix_args.txt
## from the server root.
ARGS_PATH=$(sed -n 's|.*@\(libraries/net/neoforged/neoforge/[^/]*/unix_args\.txt\).*|\1|p' run.sh 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)
if [ -n "${ARGS_PATH}" ] && [ -f "${ARGS_PATH}" ]; then
    echo "-- Linking ${ARGS_PATH} -> unix_args.txt --"
    ln -sf "${ARGS_PATH}" unix_args.txt
else
    echo "ERROR: the installer left no libraries/net/neoforged/neoforge/*/unix_args.txt."
    exit 1
fi

if [ ! -f server.properties ]; then
    echo "-- Writing a default server.properties --"
    printf 'enable-query=true\nserver-ip=0.0.0.0\n' > server.properties
fi

## The EULA is not accepted here: the panel's EULA feature asks the server owner
## on first start. config/multiforge-server.toml is written by the server itself
## on first boot.
mkdir -p mods config

echo "MultiForge installation complete."
